summary: Manchester punk band that paired buzzsaw guitars with tight, melodic pop songwriting. They wrote the template for pop punk.
know: Pete Shelley and Howard Devoto formed the band after seeing the Sex Pistols in 1976.
Their 1976 EP Spiral Scratch was one of the first self-released punk records in Britain.
Singles Going Steady collected their run of late-70s singles and became a pop-punk touchstone.
keyAlbums: Another Music in a Different Kitchen
songs: Ever Fallen in Love (With Someone You Shouldn't've)

influencedBy.why: Shelley and Devoto started the band after driving to London to see the Sex Pistols, then booked them in Manchester.
Shelley cited the Velvet Underground's drone and economy as a model for their guitar sound.
Raw, simple Stooges riffs were part of the band's early covers and attack.
Their short, hook-first songs draw on 60s Beatles pop craft.
Shelley named Can's repetitive grooves as an influence on his guitar playing.

cousins.why: Power pop with crunch, built on short, perfect hooks.
Relentless melodic hooks, just played much faster.
